notes.content: Contemplating a vibrant career in media, communications or journalism? Check out the MCJ Department. An exciting array of options awaits students, including advertising, broadcast journalism, film and media arts, digital journalism and public relations. Broadcast Journalism. Broadcast journalism students learn the importance of producing responsible news coverage while maintaining strong ethical standards. Our program’s core focuses on teaching the principles of storytelling through video, audio, and powerful writing. Our students learn through their experiences, which include producing content for television, radio, and digital platforms in English and Spanish. Broadcast journalism graduates are now reporters, producers, and anchors at local and national radio and television stations. Other alumni have embarked on careers at technology and social media companies including Google, Amazon, Facebook, and Banjo. Majors must complete a minimum of 37 semester units of mass communication and journalism courses with a grade of C or better in each course . Each student will take 19 units of MCJ core courses and 18 units of courses in their selected option. Each MCJ major must select an option, which is an area of specialization within the major. The options are advertising and public relations, broadcast and multiplatform journalism, digital journalism, and film and media arts. The courses required for each option are listed under Major Requirements. Advising Notes: MCJ majors are not permitted to enroll for CR/NC grading in MCJ courses applied to the major, except for courses that require such grading. It is recommended that students take at least 12 elective units from the following courses: MCJ 14 , MCJ 104 , MCJ 106 , MCJ 107 , MCJ 108 , MCJ 122 , MCJ 123 , MCJ 124 , MCJ 126 , MCJ 128 , MCJ 129 , MCJ 177T , MCJ 190 , MCJ 191I In addition to the major program requirements, every student must also complete the University’s baccalaureate degree requirements such as: American Government and Institutions ( PLSI 2 ) General Education Requirements (43 units) - It is recommended that students take MCJ courses for the General Education requirements package: MCJ 1 (Area 4B), MCJ 6 (Area 6), MCJ 9 (Area 3A), MCJ 183 (Area UD 3), and MCJ 101 , MCJ 175 , MCJ 178 , or MCJ 180 (Area UD 4) Additional University Graduation Requirements (9 units) - It is recommended that students take an MCJ course for the AUGR M/I requirement: MCJ 176 or MCJ 179 . Students with a declared MCJ - Broadcast and Digital Journalism major following a TMC/ADT similar pathway are exempt from 3 units of this degree requirement. Upper-Division Writing Requirement - Students must meet all university graduation requirements. This includes the Upper-Division Writing requirement, which must be met by taking MCJ 102W General Education, Additional University Graduation Requirements, and Upper-division Writing courses can be double counted with major/additional requirements. See advisor for details. Sufficient Elective Units to Meet Required Total Units (varies); it is recommended that units in this area be utilized to complete a second major or minor. A full description of the University’s graduation requirements can be found in the Baccalaureate Degree Requirements .

Advising Notes:

MCJ majors are not permitted to enroll for CR/NC grading in MCJ courses applied to the major, except for courses that require such grading.

  • It is recommended that students take at least 12 elective units from the following courses: MCJ 14, MCJ 104, MCJ 106, MCJ 107, MCJ 108, MCJ 122, MCJ 123, MCJ 124, MCJ 126, MCJ 128, MCJ 129, MCJ 177T, MCJ 190, MCJ 191I 


In addition to the major program requirements, every student must also complete the University’s baccalaureate degree requirements such as:

  • American Government and Institutions (PLSI 2)
  • General Education Requirements (43 units) - It is recommended that students take MCJ courses for the General Education requirements package: MCJ 1 (Area 4B), MCJ 6 (Area 6),  MCJ 9 (Area 3A), MCJ 183 (Area UD 3), and MCJ 101, MCJ 175, MCJ 178, or MCJ 180 (Area UD 4)
  • Additional University Graduation Requirements (9 units) - It is recommended that students take an MCJ course for the AUGR M/I requirement: MCJ 176 or MCJ 179. 
  1. Students with a declared MCJ - Broadcast and Digital Journalism major following a TMC/ADT similar pathway are exempt from 3 units of this degree requirement.  
  • Upper-Division Writing Requirement - Students must meet all university graduation requirements. This includes the Upper-Division Writing requirement, which must be met by taking MCJ 102W 
  • ﻿General Education, Additional University Graduation Requirements, and Upper-division Writing courses can be double counted with major/additional requirements. See advisor for details.
  • Sufficient Elective Units to Meet Required Total Units (varies); it is recommended that units in this area be utilized to complete a second major or minor.

A full description of the University’s graduation requirements can be found in the Baccalaureate Degree Requirements.

notes.content: Additional University Graduation Requirements The Additional University Graduation Requirements are designed to complement the GE requirements. It is the policy of Fresno State, that all students will cultivate and refine their affective, cognitive, and physical faculties through studying great works of the human imagination; be equipped for lifelong understanding and development of themselves as integrated physiological, social, and psychological beings; and be prepared to understand and live in a multicultural and international world through their undergraduate education. This will be accomplished through a total of 9 units from the following areas, each requiring 3 units: Arts/Humanities (A/H) - All students are required to take an Arts/Humanities course to graduate at the bachelor’s degree level. Lifelong-Understanding and Self-Development (L/S) - All students are required to take a lifelong understanding and self-development course to for graduate at the bachelor’s degree level. Multicultural/International (M/I) - All Students are required to take a Multicultural / International course at Fresno State to graduate at the bachelor’s degree level.

Additional University Graduation Requirements


The Additional University Graduation Requirements are designed to complement the GE requirements. It is the policy of Fresno State, that all students will cultivate and refine their affective, cognitive, and physical faculties through studying great works of the human imagination; be equipped for lifelong understanding and development of themselves as integrated physiological, social, and psychological beings; and be prepared to understand and live in a multicultural and international world through their undergraduate education.

This will be accomplished through a total of 9 units from the following areas, each requiring 3 units:

  1. Arts/Humanities (A/H) - All students are required to take an Arts/Humanities course to graduate at the bachelor’s degree level. 
  2. Lifelong-Understanding and Self-Development (L/S) - All students are required to take a lifelong understanding and self-development course to for graduate at the bachelor’s degree level. 
  3. Multicultural/International (M/I) - All Students are required to take a Multicultural / International course at Fresno State to graduate at the bachelor’s degree level.
